name: Archive mechanism selection
problem: AppCDS and the Leyden AOT cache need different JVM flags, and which one a JDK supports depends on its feature release. The JDK that runs the tool is not always the JDK that runs the application.
how: The tool first detects the target JDK from an explicit Java home, JAVA_HOME or the running JVM. It then resolves the user request (auto, appcds or aot) to one strategy. Auto means AOT on JDK 25 or later and AppCDS before that. The strategy supplies the training flag and the runtime flag.

name: Archive-ready application layout
problem: CDS and AOT archives can only reference classes that sit in ordinary JAR files on the classpath. A Spring Boot fat JAR keeps its classes and libraries in nested JARs, so an archive trained on it would hold almost nothing.
how: The tool extracts a Spring Boot JAR with the target JDK into a launcher JAR plus a lib/ directory, then launches that JAR. Other executable JARs already have the right shape and are used unchanged. The resulting runnable JAR is what training and, later, the manifest describe.

name: Training run lifecycle
problem: A server does not exit by itself, but a CDS or AOT archive is written only by a JVM that exits normally. A run must therefore be stopped at the right time, in the right way, and its result must be checked.
how: The tool starts the application with the recording flag, lets a ReadyCondition decide when startup is complete, sends SIGTERM, waits for the JVM to finish writing, then accepts the run only when the exit code is right and a non-empty archive exists. Any failed run leaves no archive.

title: A bad cache never stops an application
rule: A bad or missing cache archive must never stop an application from starting. Never pass -Xshare:on or any flag that makes the JVM fail on an archive mismatch.
why: The archive is an optimisation. A stale archive in a pod would otherwise turn a slow start into an outage.

name: Ignore-not-fail archive fallback
problem: A startup cache that is stale or mismatched must not take an application down
how: Runs use the JVM default -Xshare:auto: a mismatched archive is ignored whole and the application starts uncached; -Xshare:on is never used

name: Same-moment startup measurement
problem: Startup comparisons between variants are meaningless unless every variant is stopped at the same definition of started
how: bench reuses the exit mode's ready condition, runs fresh JVMs, discards a warm-up run and reports medians
